papers.title: Meibomian gland epithelial cells demonstrate enhanced reliance on glycolysis for energy metabolism and differentiation.
papers.authors: Ren Y, Li W, Zhang Y, Tian Y, Yi S, Tian X, Chen Y, Ke M, Xia F, Liu Y.
papers.abstract: Meibomian gland dysfunction is a leading cause of dry eye disease. Previous studies have established that the meibomian gland exists in a physiological hypoxic environment, with hypoxia-inducible factor 1α playing a regulatory role. However, the metabolic strategy of this gland remains unclear. This study aimed to test the hypothesis that glycolysis serves as an important metabolic pathway in meibomian gland epithelial cells in vivo and that these cells have an enhanced glycolytic phenotype during differentiation. We combined clinical imaging, tissue analysis, and in vitro experiments to test our hypothesis. 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography revealed significantly higher glucose uptake in human meibomian glands than in the orbicularis oculi muscle and surrounding subcutaneous connective tissues outside the tarsal plate, indicating substantial glycolytic activity in vivo. Immunofluorescence staining confirmed strong expression of glycolytic markers, including hypoxia-inducible factor 1α, glucose transporter type 1, hexokinase 2, 6-phosphofructo-2-kinase/fructose-2,6-biphosphatase 3, and pyruvate kinase M2, and lactate dehydrogenase A, in both human and mouse meibomian gland tissues. In immortalized human meibomian gland epithelial cells, differentiation induced a metabolic shift favoring glycolysis with increased extracellular acidification rate, elevated lactate production, and upregulated glycolytic enzyme expression. Three-dimensional spheroid cultures further revealed state-dependent metabolic heterogeneity. The findings indicate that meibomian gland epithelial cells have a highly glycolytic phenotype in vivo and markedly enhanced glycolytic dependence during differentiation. These support their specialized secretory functions and adaptation to hypoxic microenvironments.

papers.title: Corneal versus refractive surgically induced astigmatism: vector analysis of their dissociation and implications for toric IOL planning.
papers.authors: Kaiser KP, Wendelstein JA, Mehta JS, Wend J, Necpal P, Langenbucher A, Kohnen T.
papers.abstract: Purpose To determine whether tomographically measured surgically induced astigmatism (SIA) is reflected in the manifest refraction, and whether the ocular residual astigmatism (ORA) precedes surgery and is stable per eye. Design Single-center, longitudinal, comparative vector analysis. Methods Eyes underwent non-toric intraocular lens (IOL) or phakic implantable collamer lens (ICL) implantation. Total corneal refractive power (Pentacam) and manifest subjective refractive astigmatism at the corneal plane were expressed as Cartesian double-angle power vectors before and 3 months after surgery, yielding tomographic SIA (tSIA), refractive SIA (rSIA), their vector difference ΔSIA, and the pre- and postoperative ORA. Each SIA was decomposed into its flattening effect and torque at the incision meridian. Centroids were tested against the null by eye side. Results Of 290 eyes (256 IOL; 34 ICL), tSIA magnitude was small (IOL 0.47D; ICL 0.34-0.39D) with centroids near null. ΔSIA had a large mean magnitude (IOL 0.74-0.88D) but a near-origin centroid, significant only in IOL right eyes. Mean corneal flattening effect (+0.008D right, +0.140D left eyes) did not predict its refractive counterpart. ORA did not differ between cohorts (-0.11D, 95%-CI -0.25 to +0.02) and remained significant postoperatively, yet per eye only half the offset persisted in phakic and less in pseudophakic eyes. Conclusions The per-eye tSIA was uncorrelated with the refractive SIA and carried no systematic direction, as power vectors or flattening effect, which stayed below a quarter of a toric cylinder step. ORA preceded surgery and remained systematically stable. Individually measured tSIA has only limited value for toric IOL planning.

papers.title: Pediatric Endothelial Keratoplasty: A Modified Delphi Consensus by the EKLG Study Group on Indications, Surgical Techniques, and Postoperative Care.
papers.authors: Gupta N, Ramappa M, Serafino M, Ali A, Conner E, Hamada S, Pineda R, Busin M, Cremona F, Gimeno FL, Pereira NC, Prescott C, Romano V, Trief D, Watson SL, Wylegala E, Zaidman G, Mehta JS, Nischal KK.
papers.abstract: Purpose To identify areas of consensus among global experts on the clinical management of pediatric endothelial keratoplasty (EK), including patient selection, timing, preoperative evaluation, technique selection, intraoperative standards, and postoperative care, and to provide a practical framework for surgeons earlier in their pediatric EK learning curve. Design Modified Delphi-based global consensus study. Participants International ophthalmologists with expertise in endothelial keratoplasty and pediatric corneal diseases. Methods A series of consensus statements on pediatric EK were developed from iterative rounds of structured questions and statements posed to a panel of experts. Two rounds of asynchronous electronic questionnaires were followed by a structured hybrid discussion of unresolved items. Experts responded anonymously to statements assessing consensus and to revised items addressing indications, contraindications, timing, preoperative workup, technique selection, intraoperative standards, and postoperative management. Results are reported using item-specific denominators because occasional non-response occurred across the survey items. Main outcome measures Consensus was defined as ≥70% agreement among the experts. Agreement between 60% and 69.9% was considered to be near consensus. Results The consensus supported pediatric EK for congenital hereditary endothelial dystrophy, aphakic or pseudophakic corneal edema, persistent corneal edema in congenital glaucoma, X-linked endothelial corneal dystrophy, iatrogenic endothelial decompensation, and trauma-related decompensation. EK was inappropriate for severe anterior segment dysgenesis with keratolenticular or extensive iridocorneal adhesions. In Round 2, experts further endorsed EK for failed penetrating keratoplasty due to endothelial failure, congenital glaucoma with visually significant Haab's striae, and forceps injury involving the visual axis. There was a consensus that the timing of intervention should be guided primarily by amblyopia risk rather than by a specific age cut off. Essential preoperative assessments included examination under anesthesia, B-scan ultrasonography, anterior segment optical coherence tomography, intraocular pressure measurement, ultrasound biomicroscopy, and refraction. Experts agreed that ultrathin-DSAEK and DSAEK are the predominant techniques, whereas DMEK is currently selectively reserved, usually for older children with uncomplicated anterior segment anatomy. Preferred intraoperative principles included air tamponade, anterior chamber maintenance, and donor graft under-sizing relative to the corneal diameter. Postoperative recommendations included early intraocular pressure assessment, topical corticosteroid therapy for > 6 months, regular monitoring for steroid response, selective contact lens use, and individualized long-term follow-up. Conclusions The consensus statements provide globally endorsed recommendations for the clinical management of pediatric EK. These guidelines are relevant for corneal specialists providing a practical framework to benchmark practice, reduce variability, and guide future multicenter investigations.

papers.title: Age-dependent structural evolution of a functional amyloid contributes to memory impairment in Drosophila.
papers.authors: Ou S, Guillen-Poza PA, Ng KK, Xu L, Cheng BY, Yi Y, Ho LY, Franco-Fernández A, Khaki PSS, Mukhi M, Cheung KC, Sharma R, Oroz J, Hirano Y, Hervas R.
papers.abstract: Cryogenic electron microscopy has revealed endpoint structures of ex vivo amyloid filaments, but how amyloids assemble and evolve in living organisms-and how these transitions affect physiology-remains poorly understood. Here, we map the age-dependent structural landscape of Orb2 amyloid, a synaptic translation regulator required for long-term memory, across the adult lifespan of Drosophila melanogaster. By determining multiple Orb2 amyloid structures, we uncover a dynamic, age-linked progression of amyloid states. Translation-promoting assemblies predominate early in life, whereas aging shifts the Orb2 amyloid ensemble toward structurally distinct, destabilization-resistant assemblies with reduced translational activity, coinciding with memory impairment. Manipulating memory-related chaperones in the brain shifts Orb2 toward youthful, translation-promoting states and improves memory in old flies; conversely, shifting Orb2 toward aged-like, translation-deficient states in young adults is associated with premature memory impairment. These findings define an in vivo trajectory of amyloid evolution and link amyloid structural dynamics to synaptic translation and memory.

papers.title: Spatial single-cell mapping of transcriptional differences across genetic backgrounds in mouse brains.
papers.authors: Hemminger Z, Tam G, De Ocampo H, Wang A, Underwood T, Xie F, Zhao Q, Song D, Li JJ, Dong H, Wollman R.
papers.abstract: Genetic variation can alter organ structure and function. Comparative statistical analysis of organs across genetic backgrounds requires spatial, single-cell, atlas-scale data in replicates. Here we introduce atlas-scale transcriptome localization using aggregate signatures (ATLAS), a scalable tissue mapping method that learns transcriptional signatures from single-cell RNA sequencing data, encodes them in situ with tens of thousands of oligonucleotide probes and decodes them to infer cell types and imputed transcriptomes. We validated ATLAS against direct MERFISH measurements of marker genes and through quantitative comparisons to four other technologies. We profiled 40 million cells across more than 400 coronal sections from central brains of five male and five female C57BL/6J mice and five male BTBR T + tf/J mice, an idiopathic autism model. Our analysis revealed more than 40 significant differences in cell-type distributions and identified 16 regional composition changes across male-female and B6-BTBR comparisons. ATLAS thus enables systematic comparative studies, facilitating organ-level structure-function analysis of disease models.

papers.title: Decoder-FFPE-seq enables sensitive, genome-wide spatial transcriptomics of archival tissues at single-cell resolution.
papers.authors: Cao J, Zeng J, Meng Y, Huang S, Zhang J, Fang X, Guo Y, Shi W, Liu Y, Zheng Z, Fang J, Xiong X, Chen G, Wu L, Yang C.
papers.abstract: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue-compatible spatial transcriptomics (ST) is transforming biology and histopathology, but achieving high sensitivity, genome-wide coverage, single-cell resolution, and researcher accessibility remains challenging. To address these challenges, we here present a dendrimeric DNA coordinate barcoding design for FFPE tissue-adapted spatial RNA sequencing (Decoder-FFPE-seq) by integrating RNA-to-DNA probe conversion with blotting-assisted barcoding. Decoder-FFPE-seq provides single-cell resolution with a >2.6-fold sensitivity increase in whole-transcriptome mouse brain and archived human sample profiling over existing platforms, resolving potential cellular identity of low-abundance genes, finer tissue architecture, and capturing an epithelial-mesenchymal transition-associated signature for prognostic value. With expanded probe libraries, Decoder-FFPE-seq captures long noncoding and viral RNAs, revealing their spatial coregulatory networks with messenger RNAs in oral squamous cell carcinomas (OSCCs). In an OSCC immunotherapy cohort, two CD8 + T cell subpopulations were respectively identified in pre- and postchemoimmunotherapy samples, potentially linked to treatment response. Decoder-FFPE-seq establishes a robust, high-resolution, and accessible framework for sensitive ST profiling of archival tissues in fundamental and translational studies.

papers.title: Human hair-bearing skin organoids reveal cell type-specific susceptibility and innate immune responses to herpes simplex virus 1.
papers.authors: Wyler E, Albertini S, Friedel CC, Manukyan A, Winterfeldt A, Bracker N, Huang J, Krasemann S, Plumbom I, Altmüller J, Conrad T, Reimer R, Schneider C, Radbruch H, Hafezi W, Hansen A, Grundhoff A, Landthaler M, Fischer N, Czech-Sioli M.
papers.abstract: Epithelial surfaces are the primary sites of lytic herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) infection following initial exposure or reactivation from latency. To model this complex environment, we used human hair-bearing skin organoids and combined single-cell spatial transcriptomics with imaging to map viral spread and host responses across skin architecture. Our data suggest delayed progression of the HSV-1 life cycle in epidermal keratinocytes and hair follicle cells compared to the dermis. Infection triggered spatially organized host responses, including induction of IER3 in papillary fibroblasts. In basal keratinocytes, IRF3 was up-regulated in both infected and neighboring uninfected cells, consistent with paracrine activation of antiviral signaling. Inflammatory responses were compartmentalized in a cell type-specific manner, with TNFSF9 (4-1BBL) induced in papillary fibroblasts and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) induced in keratinocytes. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays confirmed secretion of these cytokines and the TNF-α-responsive chemokines CXCL2 and CXCL10. CXCL2 expression was enriched in cells adjacent to TNF-α-expressing cells, highlighting spatial coordination of inflammatory signaling. While interferon-β reduced viral replication, TNF-α and 4-1BBL did not, suggesting that their primary role is to orchestrate immune cell recruitment and activation. These findings establish human hair-bearing skin organoids as a physiologically relevant model for investigating spatial host-HSV-1 interactions.

papers.title: Ophthalmic Encounters After Tamoxifen Initiation.
papers.authors: Gandhi S, Balas M, Wang P, McKay BR, Kertes PJ, Martens R.
papers.abstract: Importance Tamoxifen can cause retinal toxicity and vision loss, yet no formal screening guideline exists in the US. Objective To characterize ophthalmic use after tamoxifen initiation, identify predictors, and compare 12-month use between those with breast cancer taking tamoxifen and those taking aromatase inhibitors. Design, setting, and participants This was a retrospective cohort study conducted May to June 2026 using All of Us data with 365-day minimum follow-up. The setting was a US multisite research program. Participants included adults with a first tamoxifen prescription recorded in All of Us, excluding those taking hydroxychloroquine. The comparator included those with breast cancer taking aromatase inhibitors. Exposures Tamoxifen or aromatase inhibitor initiation. Main outcomes and measures The primary outcome was any ophthalmic encounter within 12 months, identified from eye examination, retinal procedure, and eye visit codes. Retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) or fundus photography was secondary. Logistic regression assessed predictors and compared treatment groups after adjustment for demographics, preexisting conditions, preindex health care use, region, and initiation year. Results Among 2327 individuals taking tamoxifen (mean [SD] age, 53.8 [10.6] years; 2232 [95.9%] female), 162 (7.0%) had an ophthalmic encounter within 12 months, and 39 (1.7%) underwent retinal OCT or fundus photography. Among participants with preexisting glaucoma or diabetic retinopathy, 22 of 88 (25.0%) had an encounter vs 140 of 2239 (6.3%) without either condition (difference, 18.7 percentage points; 95% CI, 10.8-28.8 percentage points; P Conclusions and relevance Results of this cohort study suggest that ophthalmic use after tamoxifen initiation was uncommon, and retinal-specific testing was rare. Tamoxifen use was not associated with greater adjusted 12-month use than aromatase inhibitor use. Additional evidence on retinopathy incidence, natural history, screening strategies, and clinical benefit is needed to inform guidance.

papers.title: Bi-Allelic PRKCZ Loss-of-Function Variants and Adult-Onset Retinitis Pigmentosa.
papers.authors: Cordeddu V, Sangermano R, Mulder SWM, Hussain HMJ, Flex E, Mignini L, Motta M, Bruselles A, Arasi MB, Cecchetti S, Carvetta M, Niceta M, Lauri A, Leone A, Paradisi G, Mehta PA, Yumei L, Wang M, Zein WM, Shliaga S, Wigman LH, van Leeuwen Y, Klaver CCW, Pennings R, van den Born LI, Segrè AV, Pierce EA, Collin RWJ, Dell'Aquila C, Barbano L, Guan B, Place EM, Lin S, Webster AR, Moosajee M, Chen R, Arno G, Roosing S, Ziccardi L, Bujakowska KM, Tartaglia M.
papers.abstract: Importance Inherited retinal diseases are genetically heterogeneous disorders, with retinitis pigmentosa (RP) representing the most common form; although more than 90 genes have been implicated, many RP cases remain molecularly unsolved. Objectives To describe an adult-onset RP phenotype associated with loss-of-function variants in PRKCZ, profile the clinical features of this disorder, and investigate the underlying disease mechanism. Design, setting, and participants In this case series study, genomic analyses were performed in individuals with unsolved childhood- and adult-onset retinal disease recruited through international research and diagnostic programs. Detailed clinical characterization was conducted in affected individuals. In vitro analyses were carried out to validate the genomic findings using primary and transduced cell-based experimental approaches. Genomic analyses were performed from October 2023 to December 2025; functional studies were carried out from January 2024 to May 2026. Exposure Bi-allelic likely pathogenic variants in a novel RP disease gene candidate, PRKCZ. Main outcomes and measures The primary outcome was genetic, clinical, and functional effects of bi-allelic PRKCZ inactivating variants associated with adult-onset RP. A detailed ophthalmologic assessment was conducted to characterize the clinical phenotype. Functional analyses in patient-derived fibroblasts and transduced cell lines were performed to validate the consequence of disruptive variants on PRKCZ transcript processing and PKCζ function. Results Among approximately 4500 individuals with unsolved childhood- and adult-onset retinal disease tested, 6 bi-allelic PRKCZ variants were identified in 13 affected individuals from 10 unrelated families, 5 of which were predicted to lead to loss of function (frameshift, nonsense, or splice-altering variants). Six of 13 affected individuals (46%) were female. Most cases carried a recurrent frameshift variant (c.139_140del; p.Met47Valfs*19). All variants selectively affected the long PRKCZ transcript encoding the N-terminal Phox and Bem1 (PB1) domain. Clinically, PRKCZ-associated RP showed adult onset (18-49 years), progressive night blindness, peripheral visual field constriction, and eventual central vision loss. Four individuals exhibited adult-onset sensorineural hearing loss. Functional studies in patient-derived fibroblasts demonstrated selective loss of the long PRKCZ isoform, impaired ciliogenesis, and altered mitochondrial organization, which were validated in stable PRKCZ knockdown cell lines. Structural modeling and coimmunoprecipitation assays indicated that the missense variant was associated with the disruption of PB1 domain-mediated protein-protein interactions. Conclusions and relevance In this case series study, bi-allelic inactivating variants in PRKCZ were associated with adult-onset RP with an isoform-specific mechanism involving the long retinal-enriched transcript. These findings expand the genetic spectrum of RP and highlight PRKCZ as a potentially clinically relevant gene implicated in adult-onset retinal degeneration.

papers.title: Visual Field and RNFL OCT Testing Among Rural and Urban Residents With Glaucoma.
papers.authors: Choi S, Lin SYT, Xiao X, Singh K, Wang SY, Sight Outcomes Research Collaborative (SOURCE) Consortium.
papers.abstract: Importance Rural populations face disparities in eye care; therefore, understanding the utilization of structural imaging and visual field (VF) testing for glaucoma monitoring among rural compared with urban patients is important. Objective To evaluate whether rural residence and sociodemographic factors are associated with patterns of VF testing and retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) optical coherence tomography (OCT) in patients with glaucoma. Design, setting, and participants This retrospective longitudinal cohort study used data from the Sight Outcomes Research Collaborative (SOURCE) consortium, a multi-institutional repository of US academic ophthalmic clinical data, from May 2012 to January 2025. Included patients had at least 2 separate dates of glaucoma billing codes, at least 3 years of follow-up data, and at least 1 VF or RNFL OCT test. Exposure Rural vs urban residence, categorized by Rural-Urban Commuting Area codes. Main outcomes and measures Primary outcomes were utilization frequency (tests per year) and regular monitoring (≥1 test every 18 months) for VF and RNFL OCT. Testing frequency was analyzed using multivariable negative binomial regression, and regular monitoring was analyzed using logistic regression adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics and baseline visual acuity. Results Among 48 196 patients, 45 843 (95.1%) lived in urban areas (25 613 [55.9%] female; mean [SD] age, 67.78 [12.71] years) and 2353 (4.9%) lived in rural areas (1272 [54.1%] female; mean [SD] age, 67.3 [12.03] years). Mean (SD) VF testing frequency was 0.91 (0.52) tests per year among rural patients and 0.91 (0.56) among urban patients; rural residence was not associated with regular VF monitoring (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 0.95; 95% CI, 0.88-1.04; P = .28). Rural residence was associated with lower RNFL OCT frequency (mean [SD], 0.57 [0.45] vs 0.63 [0.47] tests per year; difference, -0.06 [95% CI, -0.08 to -0.04] tests per year; adjusted incidence rate ratio, 0.93 [95% CI, 0.88-0.98]; P = .004) and lower odds of regular RNFL OCT monitoring (AOR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.74-0.90; P Conclusions and relevance In this cohort study, rural residence was associated with lower utilization of RNFL OCT but not VF testing, while Medicaid insurance was associated with lower odds of monitoring for both modalities. The findings suggest that ophthalmologists should be aware that rural patients with glaucoma may require additional attention to continuity of structural imaging.

papers.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Paracentral Acute Middle Maculopathy for Arteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy.
papers.authors: Molleti S, Lang MV, Owosela B, Sandozi H, Henderson AD, Carey AR, Chen JJ, McClelland CM, Chodnicki KD, Tajfirouz DA, Lee MS.
papers.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of paracentral acute middle maculopathy (PAMM) detected on optical coherence tomography (OCT) macula for differentiating arteritic anterior ischemic neuropathy (AAION) from nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) in a multicenter United States cohort. Design Retrospective, multicenter diagnostic accuracy analysis. Participants This study included patients diagnosed with AAION or NAION at the University of Minnesota, Mayo Clinic, and Johns Hopkins Wilmer Eye Institute between January 2020 and January 2025. Inclusion criteria consisted of patients older than 50 years who had obtained OCT macula within 14 days of symptom onset. AAION diagnoses were confirmed by temporal artery biopsy or positron emission tomography/computed tomography. Methods Two masked fellowship-trained neuro-ophthalmologists independently evaluated OCT images for the presence of acute PAMM. Main outcome measures Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) of PAMM for AAION were calculated. Results A total of 119 patients were included, consisting of 27 patients with AAION and 92 patients with NAION. PAMM was identified in 18.5% of patients with AAION and 5.4% of patients with NAION (p = 0.032). The sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV of PAMM for AAION was 19% [95% CI: 0.08-0.37], 94.6% [95% CI: 0.88-0.98], 50% [95% CI: 0.24-0.76], and79.8% [95% CI: 0.71-0.86] respectively. Three of five NAION patients with PAMM had provoked NAION associated with severe systemic hypoperfusion. Conclusion PAMM is a highly specific but insensitive OCT marker for AAION. Although its presence should increase clinical suspicion for AAION, PAMM may rarely occur in patients with NAION particularly in the setting of systemic hypoperfusion and should be interpreted within the overall clinical context.

papers.title: Choroidal Thickness and Axial Length as Independent Correlates of AMD: Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2017-2020.
papers.authors: Choi M, Park SJ, Kim BH, Shin JP, Choi KS, Jo YJ, Park KH.
papers.abstract: Purpose To examine how choroidal thickness and axial length relate to age-related macular degeneration (AMD) across disease stages in a nationwide Korean population. Design Cross-sectional, population-based study. Methods We analyzed the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, 2017-2020, including 15,388 adults aged 40 years or older with gradable fundus photographs; ocular analyses included 13,807 after excluding coexisting macular disease. Axial length (AL), central macular thickness (CMT), and subfoveal choroidal thickness (SFCT) were measured by partial coherence interferometry and optical coherence tomography. Associations were assessed by survey-weighted logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, and systemic factors. Results Weighted AMD prevalence was 14.41% (95% CI, 13.67-15.15; early, 13.46%; late, 0.95%). In multivariable models, greater SFCT was associated with early AMD (OR per 10 µm, 1.03; 95% CI, 1.02-1.03; P Conclusions Greater SFCT and shorter AL were independently associated with early AMD. These findings suggest that choroidal thickness and axial length may reflect distinct structural correlates.

papers.title: Constructing an Objective Defocus Curve from Pyramidal Wavefront Aberrometry: Mapping Objective-to-Subjective Through-Focus Response.
papers.authors: Russo A, Versaci F, Romano V, Darcy K, Bo V, Filini O, Taylor S, Boldini A, Zilioli J, Savini G.
papers.abstract: Purpose To construct an objective defocus curve from pyramidal wavefront aberrometry and map it onto the subjective through-focus response. Design Prospective multicenter case series with external validation. Subjects, participants, and/or controls 98 eyes of 63 patients implanted with the RayOne Galaxy spiral refractive intraocular lens (IOL) at three centers (Italy, UK); 81 eyes with a wavefront pupil ≥ 4 mm were split by patient into training (56) and test (25) sets; 19 eyes with other refractive extended-depth-of-focus IOLs from a fourth center formed an external cohort. Methods, intervention, or testing Pyramidal aberrometry (Osiris) with numerically introduced defocus from +1.00 to -4.00 diopters (D); the second-moment radius of the geometrical point spread function was mapped to acuity by a rational function and compared with monocular ETDRS defocus curves. Main outcome measures Root-mean-square error (RMSE), bias, and 95% limits of agreement (LoA) between mapped objective and subjective acuity; objective versus subjective depth of field (DOFi). Results Internal test set: RMSE 0.095 logMAR (95% CI, 0.078-0.110), bias 0.016 logMAR (LoA, -0.168 to +0.201); external cohort: RMSE 0.092 logMAR (0.079-0.103), bias -0.021 logMAR (LoA, -0.197 to +0.155). Objective minus subjective DOFi at 0.20 logMAR was -0.10 D (LoA, -1.44 to +1.25 D) and -0.15 D (LoA, -0.98 to +0.69 D). Cohort-mean subjective DOFi was 2.43 D (Full-DOFi, continuous); corrected distance acuity was 20/20 or better in 88.8%. Conclusions An objective defocus curve from one pyramidal wavefront acquisition estimated the subjective through-focus response with small bias and limits of agreement of about ±0.2 logMAR in a test set and an independent cohort of refractive IOLs; individual precision, diffractive designs, and pupil-specific curves need further work.

papers.title: Retinal phenotypes and longitudinal clinical courses in patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome.
papers.authors: Kuniyoshi K, Domoto A, Hayashi T, Torii K, Suga A, Yoshitake K, Nishina S, Kondo H, Tsunoda K, Mizobuchi K, Hotta Y, Higa N, Saitsu H, Ideta S, Fukami M, Futami T, Kawashima H, Yamamura S, Kawai Y, Omae Y, Tokunaga K, Iwata T, Kusaka S.
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aimed to describe retinal phenotype, longitudinal clinical course, and genetic findings in Japanese patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome and their siblings. Design Retrospective, multicenter case series. Patients and methods This study included 12 patients with biallelic pathogenic NPHP1 variants, comprising 10 probands with symptomatic retinal dystrophy recruited from six ophthalmic centers across Japan and 2 affected siblings identified through family screening. Clinical and genetic findings were analyzed. Retinal dystrophy was diagnosed using fundus photography, fundus autofluorescence (FAF), optical coherence tomography, and electroretinography. Genetic testing was performed using whole-exome and/or whole-genome sequencing. Follow-up ranged from 0 to 44 years (mean, 14.6 years). Main outcome measures Retinal phenotype, onset of retinopathy and nephropathy, and genotype. Results Retinal phenotypes included cone/cone-rod dystrophy (4 patients), retinitis pigmentosa (4 patients), sector retinitis pigmentosa (2 patients), pigmented paravenous retinochoroidal atrophy (1 patient), and normal retina (1 patient). FAF images showed a descending tract in 5 patients. Retinopathy preceded nephropathy in 9 patients, all of whom were initially diagnosed with Leber congenital amaurosis or early-onset retinal dystrophy. Genetic testing showed that 11 patients harbored a homozygous whole-NPHP1 deletion, whereas 1 carried compound heterozygous NPHP1 and EYS variants. Conclusions Patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome showed considerable inter- and intrafamilial variability in retinal phenotype. Pigmented paravenous retinochoroidal atrophy can be associated with NPHP1 variants. A descending tract on FAF imaging may be a characteristic feature of retinal degeneration in Senior-Løken syndrome. Retinopathy, which commonly manifests as Leber congenital amaurosis or early-onset retinal dystrophy, often precedes nephropathy in patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome.

papers.title: Meibomian Gland IL-17 Expression Is Associated with Gland Dysfunction Following Corneal Nerve Injury.
papers.authors: Lin YF, Yu YS, Hsu WC, Kuo YS, Tsai WC, Chang JY, Fang WC, Fan NW.
papers.abstract: Purpose To investigate the impact of corneal nerve injury on meibomian glands (MG) and elucidate underlying mechanisms. Methods Using a murine unilateral corneal trephination model, we evaluated nerve density (βIII-tubulin), MG lipogenesis, cytokine expression (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α, IL-17), inflammatory cell infiltration, and apoptosis at 2 weeks. Inflammatory cells in tarsal plates and effector T cells in eye-draining lymph nodes (DLN) were quantified by flow cytometry. Human MG epithelial cells (HMGECs) were treated with IL-17 to assess lipogenic genes, PPAR-γ, pAkt/Akt, and inflammatory markers. IL-17 was blocked in vivo by intraperitoneal injection. In humans, MG function was compared between post-refractive surgery patients and age-matched controls. Results Trephined eyes showed reduced nerve density and lipogenesis with increased apoptosis and CD45 + cell infiltration at 2 weeks, without significant increases in CD4 + IFN-γ + or CD4 + IL-17 + T cells in DLN. Immunohistochemistry showed increased MG IL-17 expression, whereas IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α were unchanged. CD45 - IL-17 + cells, rather than CD45 + IL-17 + cells, were increased in tarsal plates. In vitro, IL-17 treatment decreased cell viability and the pAkt/Akt ratio at intermediate status, suppressed FABP4 gene expression and PPAR-γ protein, and upregulated CXCL2, IL-1β, and IL-8 in differentiated cells. In vivo IL-17 blockade reduced CD45 + cell infiltration and restored lipogenesis. In humans, 30 post-refractive surgery eyes showed reduced MG expressibility (P=0.021), worse meibum quality (P Conclusion Our data suggest that MG IL-17 expression increases following corneal nerve injury and may contribute to gland dysfunction. Targeting IL-17 may benefit patients with post-surgical MG dysfunction.

papers.title: Innate sensor responses set a supra-unitary threshold for viral replication.
papers.authors: Mukai K, Jia D, Panigrahi M, Tayman T, Brogden G, Chen YH, Haque N, Arora G, Mutterperl JE, Poe I, Zhang C, Islam Z, Holewinski R, Andresson T, Wu D, Piszczek G, Marcotrigiano J, Hogg JR, De Ravin SS, Malik NS, Nath A, Viktorova E, Zimina A, Belov GA, Bayyurt-Kocabaş B, Altan-Bonnet G, Altan-Bonnet N.
papers.abstract: Cells resist viral infection by triggering rapid and sensitive innate immune responses, initiated by cytoplasmic viral sensor proteins (CyVSP), retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I), melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (MDA-5), and protein kinase R (PKR). Our single-cell analysis reveals that viral replication requires a supra-unitary viral genome input, significantly more than one, which we define as the virion input threshold for replication (VITREP). This threshold varies depending on viruses and cell types, independently of viral protein synthesis. Through mathematical modeling and experimental testing, we uncover that supra-unitary viral genome quantities activate negative feedback regulators (NFR) of CyVSP, including death-associated protein kinase 1 (DAPK1), Rio kinase 3 (RIOK3), and protein phosphatase 2 regulatory subunit alpha (PPP2R2A), that suppress innate immune responses and allow replication. We validate key predictions of our model, namely that downregulating NFR reduces replication, whereas upregulating NFR or coinfecting cells promotes replication. Together, these findings reveal a fundamental mechanism governing viral infectivity and tissue tropism.

papers.title: Genetic coupling of floral rewards and signals underlies pollinator attraction.
papers.authors: Tan FQ, Slavkovic F, Zhang M, Adam G, Troadec C, Jiang ZH, Verdenaud M, Shirazi Parsa H, Cuzzi D, Liu X, Li X, Devani RS, Yan Y, Chen Q, Huang Y, Morison N, Zhang S, Marcel F, Gilard F, Gakiere B, Latrasse D, Benhamed M, Carcaud J, Sandoz JC, Vaissiere B, Boualem A, Dogimont C, Bendahmane A.
papers.abstract: Animal pollinators underpin biodiversity and global agriculture, yet the molecular mechanisms that coordinate floral rewards and signals to attract pollinators remain poorly understood. Through phenotyping melon genetic diversity, we identified nectarless1 (nls1), encoding the YABBY-family transcription factor YABBY5 (YAB5), as a central integrator of pollinator-attracting traits. YAB5 interacts with CRABS CLAW (CRC) during nectary initiation to specify nectary identity by repressing alternative floral organ fates. As flowers mature, YAB5 directly activates 4-α-glucanotransferase 2 (DPE2) to promote starch remobilization required for nectar secretion and promotes petal growth and flower opening. In petals, YAB5 directly engages an MYB111-dependent flavonoid pathway that generates UV nectar guides, while indirectly influencing floral volatile emission. Disrupting YAB5, DPE2, or MYB111 reduces pollinator visitation. Together, these findings reveal how a developmental regulator couples organ specification with organ-specific metabolic programs to synchronize floral rewards and signals at anthesis.

papers.title: Data-driven discovery and rapid, direct synthesis of MXenes.
papers.authors: Shamshirgar AS, Portugal GR, Ershadrad S, Ivanov R, Dahlqvist M, Chabanais F, Chakraborty S, Traksmaa R, Jussila T, Karppinen M, Hussainova I, Heintz F, Persson POÅ, Rosen J.
papers.abstract: MXenes are a rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides, yet scalable synthesis routes remain limited and historical reports suggest a broader, largely unexplored chemical space. We used machine learning-assisted database mining to uncover hidden multilayer MXenes. Screening reveals 33 previously synthesized but unrecognized MXene candidates. Guided by these findings, we synthesized seven multilayer MXenes using a rapid, scalable self-propagating high-temperature method that requires no sustained external heating and completes within minutes. We further realized 11 previously unexplored rare earth-based MXenes (M = praseodymium, neodymium, samarium, gadolinium, terbium, holmium, and thulium). Experiments and modeling suggest semiconducting behavior and diverse magnetic states across this family. Together, these results expand the MXene family and demonstrate a data-driven strategy for accelerating materials discovery through sustainable methods.

papers.title: Papaver self-incompatibility is controlled by two multiallelic idiomorphs.
papers.authors: Jin K, Du Z, Xiong T, Leng F, Liu J, Zhang M, Tian B, Hu J, Hu H, Wang W, Zhao T, Xue JY, Yang X, Ye K, Li C, Wang X, Wang X, Wang X, Chai L, Xu Q, Sun M, Franklin-Tong VE, Igić B, Jiao WB, Lin Z.
papers.abstract: Self-incompatibility (SI) prevents self-fertilization through highly polymorphic genetic recognition at the S locus with multiple alleles. In Papaver rhoeas , the S determinants were previously identified as PrpS and PrsS . However, we found that PrpS-PrsS was absent in many S haplotypes. In this work, we report the identification of an alternative pair of polymorphic S genes, S locus oligopeptide transporter ( SOPT ) and S locus glycine-rich protein ( SGRP ), segregating at the S locus when PrpS-PrsS is absent. SOPT and SGRP display hallmark S determinant features and confer SI when heterologously expressed in Arabidopsis thaliana . Therefore, instead of having allelomorphs with homologous variants, the Papaver SI system is determined by two multiallelic idiomorphs sharing no obvious common ancestry. This discovery of a dual-idiomorph system reveals a distinct genetic basis for polymorphism, with implications for the evolution of allorecognition mechanisms.

papers.title: Rapid longitudinal flights cause time shifts and Sun compass error.
papers.authors: Lewin P, Wynn J, Morford J, Padget O, Lancaster-Reeves L, Siddiqi-Davies K, Bailey H, Bond S, Davis M, Dean B, Fayet AL, Freeman R, Gillies N, Harris SM, Jaggers P, Kirk H, Maurice L, Morgan E, Nisbet C, Owen E, Parker J, Shoji A, Syposz M, Guilford T.
papers.abstract: Many animals use the Sun compass to guide their movement, sometimes over thousands of kilometers. Consistent use of the Sun compass relies on the endogenous clock to track the Sun's arc, yet animals traveling east-west experience time shifts, potentially causing mismatches between their internal clock and local time. Using GPS, we reveal that Manx shearwaters ( Puffinus puffinus ) experience such shifts during homing flights, generating predictable errors in Sun compass orientation. Use of the Sun compass persists even when shearwaters have access to compass-independent cues during coast following. Our findings provide a new avenue for chronobiology research in the wild, suggesting that rapid longitudinal movements may affect other processes governed by the endogenous clock and that conserved chronobiological mechanisms impose substantial constraints on navigation.

papers.title: Western Pacific double subduction drives Gulf of California rifting.
papers.authors: Gianni GM, He X, Becker TW, Faccenna C.
papers.abstract: Continental rifting reflects the balance between tectonic forces and lithospheric strength, yet the mechanisms of breakup remain debated. Rapid rifting of the Gulf of California oblique rift (GOCOR) ~6 million to 8 million years ago is a key example; it may have resulted from the lithosphere responding to external kinematics or acceleration of long-lived extension. The dynamics of either scenario remain incompletely understood. In this study, we highlight that the rapid rifting of the GOCOR coincides with the initiation of Western Pacific double subduction. Using three-dimensional geodynamic models, we show that such subduction reorganization can transmit extensional stresses of ~5 to 15 megapascals across the Pacific plate, loading the GOCOR and the southern San Andreas fault. Subduction reorganization may represent the missing driver for the initiation of rapid GOCOR rifting within a preconditioned lithosphere and may be an overlooked tectonic force behind other rifting events.

papers.title: Stimulated protein degradation to promote mitochondrial function and neuronal survival.
papers.authors: Chandrasekhar S, McMinimy R, Manford AG, Wehri E, Gee CL, Miller C, Bingol B, Kuriyan J, Schaletzky J, Rapé M.
papers.abstract: Targeted protein degradation is a promising modality to treat cancer or inflammation, but whether it can provide a similar benefit for disorders caused by pervasive protein dysregulation is unclear. We describe stimulated protein degradation (SPD) as a strategy that leverages agonists of stress-responsive E3 ubiquitin ligases to simultaneously eliminate multiple pathogenic factors. Specifically, we show that activators of the reductive stress response E3 CUL2 FEM1B boost degradation of multiple physiological substrates to improve mitochondrial import and electron transport chain assembly. In this manner, CUL2 FEM1B agonists preserve mitochondrial function and neuronal survival in models of neurodegenerative COX deficiency syndrome and Friedreich's ataxia. By activating E3 ligases that evolved to safeguard cellular integrity, SPD expands the use of compound-induced protein degradation to complex pathologies of high unmet need.

papers.title: A commensally regulated immune rheostat fine-tunes skin barrier fitness.
papers.authors: Gola A, Srinivas R, Rodig EG, Schernthanner M, Abdusselamoglu MD, Tierney MT, Alexander NJ, Gonzales KAU, Sajjath SM, Soto-Ugaldi LF, Bonny AR, Fuchs E.
papers.abstract: At the skin's surface, the epidermis must balance stem cell renewal with barrier maintenance to withstand environmental stress and shield against pathogens. In this study, we identify a microbial-immune-epithelial feedback mechanism that integrates environmental information into stem cell regulation in mice. Specifically, we show that Langerhans cells (LCs), an intraepithelial macrophage population, orchestrate this circuit by producing prostaglandin E 2 , which restrains stem cell proliferation, promotes epidermal differentiation, and maintains barrier integrity during homeostasis. Upon pathway disruption, stem cells become overactivated, hindering terminal differentiation and weakening barrier function. Upstream, LC activity is tuned by the local microbial environment in a rheostat-like fashion, coupling commensal sensing to stem cell dynamics. Our findings provide a general framework for how barrier tissues achieve adaptive homeostasis amid continual external fluctuations.

papers.title: Pervasive patterns in bird songs resemble those in human speech and song and are independent of vocal learning.
papers.authors: James LS, Oudyk K, Pescaru MI, Wall EM, Chen Y, Pearse WD, Sakata JT.
papers.abstract: Bird songs are often described as analogs to human speech and songs, but expansive comparisons are necessary to determine analogy and mechanistic substrates. By analyzing global corpora consisting of 367 bird species (>74,500 vocal elements from ~5900 songs) within two clades of vocal learners (oscines and hummingbirds) and related nonlearners (suboscines and nightjars) and 52 human languages (>15,000 elements in >800 speech or song phrases), we revealed common patterns in bird songs that resemble prevalent patterns in human speech and song with variation in resemblance to speech or song. Vocal learning did not systematically affect acoustic patterning or similarity to human vocalizations. These data underscore the deep analogies between bird and human vocalizations and convergent motor mechanisms shaping communication.

papers.title: Intrinsic gestational timing governs human cerebellar development after preterm birth.
papers.authors: Sanidas G, Simonti G, Ghaemmaghami J, Woyshner K, Polyviou A, Vidva R, Lowe C, Vij A, Bittel D, Triantafyllou M, Wolff N, Cardenas R, Chen H, Almeida F, Sudhakar S, Mankad K, Koutroulis I, Pettersen HS, Stein-O'Brien G, Sidiropoulos DN, Gallo V, Kratimenos P.
papers.abstract: Intrinsic programs shape brain maturation; however, which of these programs are perturbed by prematurity as well as the molecular pathways involved remain unknown. The human cerebellum serves as a paradigm of extrauterine development-its accelerated growth and circuit formation align with the third trimester, a period disrupted by preterm delivery. Using multimodal datasets encompassing in vivo neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental outcomes with postmortem spatial-transcriptomic and histopathological profiling, we show that prematurity diverts the cerebellar developmental trajectory. Cerebellar growth and functional outcomes scaled with gestational age, despite modifying perinatal exposures. Spatially resolved developmental programs underlying macroscopic trajectories were marked by incomplete granule cell maturation and impaired Purkinje cell structural refinement, which indicate lineage-specific developmental asynchrony. Thus, prematurity constitutes biologically displaced maturation, in which infants of equivalent postmenstrual age occupy divergent developmental states.
